snippet.title: Clayface | Final Trailer
snippet.description:
In four weeks, look fear in the face. #ClayfaceMovie - only in theaters October 23.

DC Studios’ “Clayface” is a horror thriller from director James Watkins, starring Tom Rhys Harries in the title role of the cult favorite villain from Gotham’s rogues gallery.

Matt Hagen’s meteoric rise from Gotham street kid to Hollywood leading man is tragically cut short when a local crime boss’s actions leave him horribly disfigured. Abandoned by his team and with nothing left, Matt seeks out a cutting edge treatment that miraculously returns him to his former self… but also unexpectedly affects his grip on reality, spiraling him down a destructive path of all-consuming revenge.

The film also stars Naomi Ackie, David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan, as well as Nancy Carroll and Joshua James.

James Watkins directs from a screenplay by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, story by Flanagan, based on characters from DC. The film is produced by Matt Reeves, Lynn Harris, James Gunn and Peter Safran, with Michael E. Uslan, Chantal Nong Vo, Lars P. Winther, Paul Ritchie, Rafi Crohn and Trevor Macy executive producing.

Watkins’ creative team includes director of photography Rob Hardy, production designer James Price, editor Jon Harris and costume designer Keith Madden. Music is by Volker Bertelmann.

DC Studios Presents a 6th & Idaho Production, a James Watkins Film, “Clayface.” The film will be distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures and released only in theaters in North America on October 23, 2026, and internationally beginning 21 October 2026.

snippet.description:
Godzilla Minus Zero (2026) ist die direkte Fortsetzung des Oscar-prämierten „Godzilla Minus One“. Regisseur, Autor und VFX-Künstler Takashi Yamazaki kehrt ebenso zurück wie Ryûnosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe und weitere Mitglieder des ursprünglichen Casts. Die Geschichte setzt 1947 ein, zwei Jahre nach den Ereignissen des Vorgängers. Seht hier den Trailercheck.

INFOS ZUM FILM
Regie: Takashi Yamazaki
Drehbuch: Takashi Yamazaki
Besetzung:
Ryûnosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yamada Yuki, Munetaka Aoki, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Kuranosuke Sasaki, Sakura Ando

Inhalt:
Japan im Jahr 1947: Zwei Jahre nach den Ereignissen von „Godzilla Minus One“ setzt die Geschichte um Koichi Shikishima, Noriko Oishi und die Überlebenden der ersten Godzilla-Katastrophe ein.
Takashi Yamazaki führt die Geschichte seines international gefeierten Vorgängers unmittelbar fort und übernimmt erneut nicht nur Regie und Drehbuch, sondern auch die Verantwortung für die visuellen Effekte. Für „Godzilla Minus One“ wurde Yamazakis VFX-Team 2024 mit dem Oscar ausgezeichnet.

snippet.title: Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour (Philadelphia Freedom Cut Part 2)
snippet.description:
Bruce Springsteen and The E Street Band have released the second part of their Philadelphia Freedom Cut project, sharing official video of the next seven songs from their Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour finale: “The Promised Land,” “Two Hearts,” “Hungry Heart,” “Youngstown,” “Murder Incorporated,” “American Skin (41 Shots)” and “Long Walk Home.”

Musicians on stage for the Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour included The E Street Band’s Roy Bittan (piano, synthesizer), Nils Lofgren (guitar, vocals), Garry Tallent (bass guitar), Stevie Van Zandt (guitar, vocals) and Max Weinberg (drums) with Soozie Tyrell (violin, guitar, vocals), Jake Clemons (saxophone) and Charlie Giordano (organ, keyboards, accordion). They were joined by The E Street Horns and Percussion (Anthony Almonte, Barry Danielian, Eddie Manion, Ozzie Melendez, Curt Ramm) and The E Street Choir (Ada Dyer, Curtis King, Lisa Lowell, Michelle Moore). Tom Morello performed with Springsteen and The E Street Band for each of the tour’s shows as a special guest.

Bruce Springsteen and The E Street Band’s “Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour: Philadelphia Freedom Cut Part 2” is directed by Chris Hilson and Thom Zimny, edited by Zimny and Sam Shapiro, and produced by Bruce Springsteen, Jon Landau, Zimny and Adrienne Gerard. Sound was mixed by Jon Altschiller and recorded by John Cooper, with lighting design by Jeff Ravitz and Todd Ricci. The project is released in memory of Dave Marsh.

“The Promised Land,” “Two Hearts,” “Hungry Heart,” “Youngstown,” “Murder Inc.,” “American Skin,” and “Long Walk Home” written by Bruce Springsteen.  
Published by Eldridge Publishing Co. and Sony Pop Music Publishing (GMR).

“It Takes Two” written by Sylvia Moy and William Stevenson.  Published by Stone Agate Music (BMI)

Photo of Dave Marsh Courtesy of Danny Clinch
